10667884_93e9e962.text: Orexins A and B (also known as hypocretins 1 and 2) are neuropeptides that consist of 33 and 28 amino acids, respectively, both of which are derived from preproorexin (46271203)(Lecea et al., 1998). Orexin neurons are mainly located in the lateral hypothalamus, from which they send axons to various regions of the brain (46271203)(Peyron et al., 1998). The hypothalamic orexins play a key role in arousal, and the loss of the orexin gene function or orexin-producing neurons causes narcolepsy in humans and rodents (Scammell et al., 2011). Orexins produces these effects through the Gq protein-coupled receptors, orexin-1 and orexin-2 receptors, which are widely expressed in the brain (Scammell et al., 2011)(Sakurai, 2014).
